summary: @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-charts preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated payload
details: Package published under the @servicetitan scope advertises itself as a React amCharts wrapper, but its actual on-install behavior is a dropper. package.json declares scripts.preinstall=node setup.mjs; setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<arch>.zip, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods +x, then execFileSyncs math_init.js under that freshly-downloaded runtime. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated bundle (obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation, hex-named identifiers, 1000+ entry constant pool). The library entry that would normally hold amCharts wrapper code — dist/index.js — is 82 bytes, so the package has no legitimate runtime; the preinstall payload is its only real behavior. Executing an opaque obfuscated bundle under an alternate runtime (Bun) is a known dropper pattern used to evade Node-oriented scanners. The @servicetitan scope name plus a CHANGELOG referencing servicetitan/hammer indicate scope impersonation of an internal ServiceTitan library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
